says: Deleting a key opens a dialog with three choices; nothing is confirmed until one is selected, and Escape cancels. Purge empties the key: all its values are destroyed and the key is marked cleared. Clear-first does the same, but first drops the key's old cleared mark so the new one sorts ahead of the values, then puts back the key's own values listed one level directly below it, skipping deletion markers and sub-key values. Delete-one writes a deletion entry for a typed value name and keeps the key's other contents; it is confirmed only when a name is typed, otherwise the person is told "You must enter a value name." and the dialog stays open. After any choice the list is rebuilt and the key is selected.

The download copies the main definition files, then the language folder named after the person's regional-format setting in Windows (not the display language) if the package has one; a missing own-language folder is skipped. When that setting is not en-US it also copies the en-US folder as a fallback, and here the folder is required: if the package lacks it, the download fails at "move the ADMX files".

Using Forget on a key asks "Are you sure you want to remove this key and all its contents?"; on No nothing changes. On Yes the key, all its sub-keys, their values and clearances are removed from the file, the list is rebuilt and the key's parent is selected (its ancestors are selected in turn). A top-level key has no parent, so nothing is selected and the buttons are refreshed to match.

Value data is requested in a dialog suited to the kind: text for string and expandable string, a number for 32-bit and 64-bit numbers, lines for multi-string. Any other kind is refused with "This value kind is not supported.". When the person cancels a dialog, or the kind is refused, no data is returned and callers change nothing.

If any step fails, the download stops, the dialog becomes idle again and the person is told "Failed to " followed by the step that failed ("create a scratch space", "download the package", "extract the package", "take control of the destination", "move the ADMX files" or "remove temporary files"), ending with a period. Nothing is rolled back: files already moved into the destination stay, and the scratch folder is deleted only as the last step, so an earlier failure leaves it behind. A failure at "remove temporary files" comes after the files were installed.

The destination text is not checked before the download starts: empty or invalid text is passed on and the download fails at "move the ADMX files". A person who is not a Windows administrator skips the ownership step and proceeds, so a protected destination fails at the move.
